title: Why your finish feels rough after one coat (and the water trick that fixes it)

slides.title: Sanded smooth. Finished rough?
slides.sub: Raise the grain before the first coat

slides.label: Why it happens
slides.heading: Water lifts the fibers
slides.body: Sanding flattens tiny wood fibers. Water-based stain or finish makes them swell and stand back up, so the surface feels fuzzy after the first coat.

slides.heading: The trick
items: Wipe the sanded wood with a damp cloth.
Let it dry completely, about an hour.
Hand sand lightly with 220 grit, with the grain.
slides.tip: Wipe off all the dust before you finish.

slides.label: Result
slides.heading: The fuzz is already gone
slides.body: The loose fibers have stood up and been sanded off. Your stain or finish goes on smooth instead of rough.
slides.fix: Best before water-based stain, poly or paint.
